tasks.short: Select and prescribe post-anesthesia medications or treatments to patients.

steps.what: Read the post-anesthesia record, allergies and medicines already given
Name the candidate post-anesthesia drug, dose and route
List formulary conflicts for that named post-anesthesia drug
Select which post-anesthesia medications these patients should receive
Prescribe the selected post-anesthesia medications in the clinical record
Give the selected post-anesthesia treatments to these patients

tasks.design: She reads the recovery record in the {OTHER} clinical record and names the drug, the dose and the route. A formulary query in {OTHER} then lists conflicts for that named drug, does not prescribe, and does not wait. She selects the medications, prescribes them in the record, and gives the treatments. A blank drug name leaves the order in her hands.
tasks.previous_blocker: The interaction lookup sat inside the prescription, so a rule check was not split from her choice of drug.
tasks.enabler_now: The organisation already keeps a formulary that can check a named drug, dose and route. Showing that list needs no new rule engine.
tasks.still_hard: She still chooses the drug. A hit is a warning. Harm to the patient stays with the prescription she signs.
tasks.human_edge: She selects and prescribes. The conflict list does not name the drug.
tasks.altitude: The conflict list leaves her week. She still names the drug, selects the medications, prescribes them and gives the treatments. She gains no new decision right.

reach.task: Maintain the interaction, contraindication, dose and duplicate rules
reach.learn: A hit is a warning. The prescription stays hers.

evidence.claim: The G-Standaard checks interactions, contraindications, doses and duplicates. KNMP sets the content.
A prescription comes from a named practitioner under Wet BIG art. 36(14).
Providers are responsible for careful use of generative AI, and the note names medication errors from wrong registration.
Copying a named drug against a fixed interaction list does not choose the drug. This is model knowledge.

assumptions: She selects and prescribes today, so those steps keep her as the actor. The machine appears only as the future conflict list.
Structured fields she writes before the list: drug name, dose and route. The recovery record and the allergy list are already in the {OTHER} clinical record.
A blank drug name runs no list. She then looks up and prescribes by hand.
The interaction list is the organisation's existing rule set. Its runtime is not her effort. The pharmacist maintains the rules.
She still gives every treatment. The prescription stays in the clinical record. Nothing is sent outside the organisation, and no order is uploaded to an external model.
Upkeep hours are zero. There is no new rule set for her to maintain. Reading whether each hit applies to this patient is already inside the selection.
unknowns: Which extra interaction fields the local rule set requires beyond drug name, dose and route.
research_questions: Which extra interaction fields does the local rule set require beyond drug name, dose and route?

already_counted.description: Reading whether each conflict hit applies to this patient, already inside the selection.

incremental.description: The pharmacist owns the rule set. She has no new list to maintain, so upkeep hours are zero.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: the order screen already shows these hits, so most of the lookup is existing runtime and she still selects by hand. High: she names a drug the formulary can check, the list returns before she selects, and she still prescribes and gives every treatment.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Perform or evaluate diagnostic tests such as radiographs and electrocardiograms.

steps.what: Perform bedside electrocardiograms and radiographs on these patients
Read the results of these diagnostic tests on the tracing and radiograph
Evaluate what these diagnostic tests mean for this anesthetic

tasks.design: She performs the bedside electrocardiogram and the radiograph, reads the tracing and the image, and evaluates what they mean for this anesthetic. Nothing is drafted, filed or sent. A rate already on the bedside monitor in {OTHER} is existing device runtime and is not her saved time.
tasks.previous_blocker: The tracing, the image and the anesthetic reading are one bedside act. No part of that act is a record a machine can file for her.
tasks.enabler_now: Nothing new is feasible. A numeric rate on the monitor is already device runtime, and it does not shorten the reading she does.
tasks.still_hard: Placing leads, taking the radiograph at the bedside, and judging what the tracing means for this anesthetic stay hers.
tasks.human_edge: She evaluates the diagnostic tests. A displayed rate is not that evaluation.
tasks.altitude: Nothing leaves her week. She still performs the tests, reads the results and evaluates them. She gains no new decision right.

reach.task: Take the radiograph when it is not done at the bedside
reach.learn: The anesthetic reading of the image stays hers.

evidence.claim: Evaluating a tracing or a radiograph for this anesthetic is her judgement. This is model knowledge.
A rate already shown on the monitor is existing device runtime and is not her labour. This is model knowledge.

assumptions: She performs the tests and evaluates them today, so every step keeps her as the actor. No machine step is added.
A numeric rate already on the bedside monitor is existing device runtime and is not counted as saved labour.
Nothing is drafted, filed or sent. Upkeep hours are zero because nothing new is built.
unknowns: Whether the bedside monitor already stores numeric intervals from the electrocardiogram.
research_questions: Does the bedside monitor already store numeric intervals, or only a live tracing?

incremental.description: Nothing is built, so upkeep hours are zero.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low and high are zero. She still performs the electrocardiogram and the radiograph, reads them, and evaluates them for this anesthetic. A rate already on the monitor is existing device runtime.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Select, order, or administer pre-anesthetic medications.

steps.what: Read the pre-anesthetic assessment, allergies and planned procedure
Name one pre-anesthetic medication, its dose and its route
List conflicts for that named pre-anesthetic medication only
Select the pre-anesthetic medication after reading each conflict
Order that selected pre-anesthetic medication in the clinical record
Administer the pre-anesthetic medication herself at the bedside

tasks.design: She reads the pre-anesthetic assessment and names one drug, dose and route. A formulary query in {OTHER} lists conflicts for that drug and never draws up a syringe. She selects it, orders it in the {OTHER} clinical record, and administers it herself. A blank name leaves the order in her hands.
tasks.previous_blocker: Drawing up the pre-anesthetic drug was one act, so a conflict list was not split from the syringe.
tasks.enabler_now: The same existing formulary query can run on one named pre-anesthetic drug before she orders it.
tasks.still_hard: She still draws up and gives the drug in the room. The list never chooses the dose.
tasks.human_edge: She selects, orders and administers. The list does not draw up a syringe.
tasks.altitude: The conflict list leaves her week. She still names the drug, selects it, orders it and administers it. She gains no new decision right.

reach.task: Keep the pre-anesthetic interaction rules current
reach.learn: A conflict hit is a warning. He does not change the drug she named.

evidence.claim: The G-Standaard checks interactions, contraindications, doses and duplicates. KNMP sets the content.
A prescription comes from a named practitioner under Wet BIG art. 36(14).
Listing conflicts for a named pre-anesthetic medication does not draw it up or administer it. This is model knowledge.

assumptions: She selects, orders and administers today, so those steps keep her as the actor. The machine appears only as the future conflict list.
Structured fields she writes before the list: drug name, dose and route. A blank name runs no list, and she orders by hand.
The interaction list is the organisation's existing rule set. Its runtime is not her effort.
The list never draws up a syringe. Giving the drug stays in the room and is not a send outside the organisation.
No order is uploaded to an external model. The clinical record stays inside the organisation.
Upkeep hours are zero. This reuses the formulary query. She maintains no second rule set.
unknowns: Whether a standing pre-anesthetic protocol already shows the same hits on the order screen.
research_questions: Does the order screen already show interaction hits for the pre-anesthetic drugs she names?

already_counted.description: Judging whether each pre-anesthetic conflict applies to this patient, already inside the selection.

incremental.description: The query is the same formulary list. There is no extra upkeep, so hours are zero.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: a standing pre-anesthetic order already shows the hits, so the list rarely replaces a search. High: she names one drug, the list returns before she selects, and she still orders and administers it herself.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: Observe patients in post-anesthesia care before any discharge
State pass or fail for each local discharge criterion
Decide whether to discharge these patients from post-anesthesia care
Write only the accepted discharge findings into the clinical record

tasks.design: She observes the patient and states pass or fail for each local discharge criterion. She decides fitness only after those findings match the patient. A write in the {OTHER} clinical record then places only the accepted findings. A rejection writes nothing. She still tells the receiving nurse in the room.
tasks.previous_blocker: The discharge note was written in the same moment as the fitness decision, so the record write was not split from the judgement.
tasks.enabler_now: Pass or fail on a local criterion is a structured field. Placing accepted fields into the clinical record is a write, not a decision.
tasks.still_hard: Whether the patient may leave stays her judgement. A scored form the ward still wants is not replaced.
tasks.human_edge: She decides discharge. The record write cannot decide fitness.
tasks.altitude: Only writing the accepted discharge record leaves her week. She still observes the patient and decides discharge. She gains no new decision right.

reach.task: Receive the patient on the ward after post-anesthesia care
reach.learn: The ward takes the patient only after the accepted discharge record is written, and the fitness decision was hers.

evidence.claim: Placing stated discharge findings into the record does not decide whether the patient may leave. This is model knowledge.
Solely automated care decisions need an art. 22(2) basis.
A person deciding discharge, then a write of findings she already accepted, is not a solely automated decision. This is model knowledge.

assumptions: She files the discharge record today, so the write keeps her as the actor. The machine is only the future of that filing.
Structured fields she states before the write: discharge criterion and pass or fail. A blank finding runs no write. She then files by hand.
She decides discharge only after the findings match the patient. A rejection writes nothing. A change to the findings voids the acceptance.
There is no second write of the same findings by hand after the accepted record is placed.
She still tells the receiving nurse in the room. That talk is not a send outside the organisation. The clinical record stays inside the organisation.
Upkeep hours are zero. The recovery unit owns the criterion list. There is no new list for her to maintain, and nothing is uploaded to an external model.
unknowns: Whether the ward expects a scored discharge form in addition to pass or fail on each criterion.
research_questions: Does the ward expect a scored discharge form beyond pass or fail on each local criterion?

already_counted.description: Matching the stated findings to this patient before discharge, already inside the decision.

incremental.description: The recovery unit owns the criterion list. She adds no upkeep, so hours are zero.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: the ward still wants a scored discharge form, so she files most of it by hand. High: pass or fail on local criteria is enough and the accepted record write fires, while she still observes the patient and decides discharge. Creating the record is a small part of the task, so the high end stays under the write's full share.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: Conflict lookup on a drug she named, and the discharge-record write, leave her week. She still selects, prescribes, gives, evaluates diagnostic tests, and decides discharge. She gains no new decision right.
skills_to_grow: Read a conflict hit as a warning, and still choose and prescribe the drug herself.
Keep the anesthetic reading of a tracing and a radiograph in her own hands.
State discharge findings so the record write cannot decide fitness.
role.ambitious_version: The week does not grow. She does not take more patients because a conflict list appears or a discharge record is written for her.
